chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Ibrahim ibn Maymoun, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who becomes junub at night during the month of Ramadan, so he forgot to perform ghusl until a week had passed, or the month of Ramadan ended. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the making up of the prayer and the fast.'

key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: Becomes junub (enters a state of major ritual impurity)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who forgets to perform ghusl and misses prayers and fasting until Ramadan ends?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that neglecting ghusl due to forgetfulness does not invalidate the fast itself, but rather creates a debt of missed prayers and the fast day that must be compensated later. This ruling highlights the Shia distinction between the validity of the fast (which remains intact despite the impurity) and the obligation of the specific acts of worship missed during the period of neglect. It underscores the principle that major ritual impurity (junub) is a state of being rather than a direct nullifier of the fast, provided one remembers to fast.
